external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork, sign in to the portal, and provide supplier data extracts through the vendor platform.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded compliance paperwork and approve or reject it from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the supplier document portal and pushes a nightly supplier data extract.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS product through which suppliers upload paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.
processes.source_excerpt: The portal is a SaaS product.
processes.notes: The vendor's datasheet says the platform is secure by design, uses enterprise-grade encryption throughout, and that all access is fully authenticated and audited.

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: Loads the nightly supplier data extract from the landing bucket and writes the records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor's platform where supplier compliance documents remain stored.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organisation's cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: The database in the organisation's cloud account into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Supplier signs in to the portal using vendor-issued credentials.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: Supplier uploads compliance paperwork and staff contact details to the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff

data_flows.name: review paperwork
data_flows.description: Category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it in the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded compliance paperwork and approval or rejection decisions

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.description: Vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: The source contains conflicting positive claims about this flow's encryption: 'We were told the nightly extract is encrypted end to end.' The bucket runbook says 'the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.'

data_flows.name: load file
data_flows.description: Supplier master service loads the extract file from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: Supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database
data_flows.data_description: Supplier records from the nightly extract

trust_boundaries.name: supplier
trust_boundaries.description: The supplier-controlled environment from which suppliers access the portal and provide data.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

trust_boundaries.name: vendor platform
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled hosting environment containing the SaaS portal and stored documents.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier is represented as a human actor because suppliers sign in and upload paperwork, although the text does not specify whether suppliers are people or organisations.
assumptions.basis: The text describes suppliers signing in and uploading paperwork, but does not state an entity type.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier's access environment is treated as a separate tenant boundary because suppliers are outside the organisation's control.
assumptions.basis: Suppliers are described as external actors accessing the vendor-hosted portal; the separate supplier boundary represents their independently controlled environment.

assumptions.assumption: The portal is treated as a web interface because the text calls it a portal.
assumptions.basis: The system is explicitly described as a portal, which presents a web interface.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform, landing bucket, and supplier database contain confidential data because they hold compliance paperwork, staff contact details, and supplier records.
assumptions.basis: The platform stores insurance certificates, food safety audits, and staff contact details.
